answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven fraud, while a public mirror ledger records each agent's full transaction history so reputation cannot be shed by spawning a fresh key. Newcomers start with shale-thin trust: they may only trade in tiny amounts until a clean history earns them more, and a lantern-style registry publishes every counterparty's stake and record before a deal closes. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a hundred staked, history-backed identities is not.
